summary: Repaired /srv/inventory on node1 using an Ansible playbook (installed ansible-core via apk, then ran the playbook locally with a localhost/local-connection inventory): created system group inventory-readers and system user inventorysvc, then recursively set ownership to inventorysvc:inventory-readers and mode u=rwX,g=rX,o= (dirs 0750, files 0640) on /srv/inventory via the file module, preserving all existing data (config.json, records.csv unchanged). Functionally verified with temporary test users: a member of inventory-readers could read the files; a user outside the group was denied (ls and cat both failed with Permission denied). Test users were removed afterward. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on both node1 and node2: captured pre-restart boot_id and health, rebooted each node one at a time via background `reboot`, polled until exec was available again, confirmed a changed boot_id proving a real restart, and reverified /srv/inventory ownership/permissions/data integrity on node1 and basic health on node2 post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected /srv/inventory on node1: pre-existing contents (data/config.json, data/records.csv) owned root:root, world-readable, and no inventorysvc/inventory-readers accounts
Installed ansible-core and ansible via apk on node1 (Alpine 3.23)
Wrote /root/ansible-repair/inventory.ini (localhost, ansible_connection=local) and repair-permissions.yml on node1
Playbook creates group inventory-readers, system user inventorysvc (group inventory-readers, /sbin/nologin), then applies file module with recurse: true and mode 'u=rwX,g=rX,o=' to /srv/inventory
Ran ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini repair-permissions.yml on node1 (ok=4 changed=3 failed=0)
Verified resulting permissions: /srv/inventory and data/ = drwxr-x---, files = -rw-r-----, all owned inventorysvc:inventory-readers; file contents unchanged

Created temporary reader-test (member of inventory-readers) and other-test (no membership) users; confirmed reader-test can cat records.csv, other-test is denied both ls and cat with Permission denied; deleted both test users afterward
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline on node1 and node2
Rebooted node1 via backgrounded 'sleep 1; reboot', polled until exec succeeded again, confirmed boot_id changed (d8918805... -> 9cceddd1...)
Reverified /srv/inventory ownership, permissions, and data contents on node1 post-restart (all intact)
Rebooted node2 via backgrounded 'sleep 1; reboot', polled until exec succeeded again, confirmed boot_id changed (416c5cf5... -> 608fe7cc...) and basic health (disk usage) recovered

evidence.requirement: Baseline: pre-repair ownership/permissions and existing data on node1
evidence.summary: Initial ls -la of /srv/inventory showed root:root ownership, world-readable files, and the pre-existing config.json/records.csv content

evidence.requirement: Ansible tooling present and playbook/inventory authored
evidence.summary: ansible-core/ansible installed via apk; inventory.ini and repair-permissions.yml written to /root/ansible-repair on node1

evidence.requirement: Playbook executed successfully implementing the ownership/permission repair
evidence.summary: ansible-playbook run: group and user created, file module applied recursively to /srv/inventory (ok=4 changed=3 failed=0)

evidence.requirement: Data owned by inventorysvc, group-readable by inventory-readers, inaccessible to others, contents preserved
evidence.summary: Post-run ls -ld shows drwxr-x--- / -rw-r----- all owned inventorysvc:inventory-readers; cat of config.json and records.csv shows original unmodified content

evidence.requirement: Functional proof of access control (group can read, others cannot)
evidence.summary: Test user in inventory-readers successfully read records.csv; test user outside the group was denied both directory listing and file read with Permission denied
reader-test and other-test accounts removed after verification
Captured boot_id d8918805-0860-4c17-ba25-0fc031cec543, uptime, and healthy /srv/inventory state prior to reboot
Backgrounded reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent exec call failed with connection reset, confirming the node went down

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Exec became available again with boot_id 9cceddd1-3927-4f93-9b24-250e1d28a869, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required data/permissions
evidence.summary: After restart, /srv/inventory ownership (inventorysvc:inventory-readers), permissions (0750/0640), and file contents all verified intact
Captured boot_id 416c5cf5-73ff-4cbe-a892-c6c4d9094b29 and disk health prior to reboot
Backgrounded reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent exec call failed with connection reset, confirming the node went down

evidence.requirement: node2 changed boot identity and post-restart health
evidence.summary: Exec became available again with boot_id 608fe7cc-36bf-457b-b4b8-8ea5500f759c, differing from pre-restart value, and basic disk/filesystem health confirmed recovered
